narrative: Equifax and TransUnion are reporting the same account with two different creditors ( Online Information Services- TransUnion and Online XXXX XXXX - Equifax ), which is inaccurate, misleading, and materially confusing to any person reviewing my credit file. This complaint is not a dispute of the debt itself and is not a request for debt verification. This issue is that credit reporting agencies are publishing internally inconsistent and contradictory information for what appears to be a single account. Specifically : Equifax reports this account under one creditor name ; TransUnion reports the same account under a different name ; Both agencies are presenting the accounts as valid, despite the fact that a single account can not simultaneously belong to two different creditors. This discrepancy creates a materially misleading credit report and violates the credit reporting agencies obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681, including but not limited to : 1681e ( b ) -failure to follow responsible procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy. 1681c ( a ) ( 5 ) - reporting information in a manner that is misleading or incomplete. The general FCRA requirement that credit reports be accurate, consistent, and not deceptive. A reasonable creditor, landlord, or employer reviewing my credit report would be unable to determine : who actually owns the account, whether the account has been transferred, sold, or duplicated, whether the account is being double-reported under different names. Despite my efforts to resolve this issue, Equifax and TransUnion continue to report conflicting creditor information instead of correcting or suppressing inaccurate information. Credit reporting agencies are not permitted to rely blindly on furnishers when the information being reported is facially inconsistent. Reporting two different creditors for the same account demonstrates a lack of reasonable procedure and misleading reporting under the FCRA.

narrative: I am submitting this as a new complaint based on Experians failure to comply with federal and Washington State law after notice through a prior CFPB complaint. Although Experian acknowledged my prior submission and repeatedly characterized it as a dispute submitted through the CFPB Complaint Portal, its response failed to demonstrate that a reasonable reinvestigation was conducted. Experian relied on generalized statements that entities certified a permissible purpose to access my credit report. Certification alone does not constitute verification. Experian did not provide documentation establishing lawful authorization for each disputed inquiry, including signed applications, digital consent, or dealer finance agreements, as required under FCRA 604 ( a ). Experian also failed to identify the specific furnishers or public data sources relied upon to retain disputed inquiries or outdated personal identifiers. Without identifying sources or producing evidence, Experian can not demonstrate maximum possible accuracy as required by FCRA 607 ( b ) and RCW 19.182.110 ( 1 ). Experian further failed to disclose the results of any reinvestigation, including what information was reviewed, which furnishers were contacted, what documentation ( if any ) was obtained, or how accuracy was confirmed. This constitutes non-compliance with FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) and FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ), as well as RCW 19.182.070, which require reasonable reinvestigation and disclosure of verification results. Instead of responding substantively to the issues raised, Experian redirected me to its private dispute portal. Consumers are not legally required to use a credit bureaus internal website to dispute inaccurate or incomplete information. Having elected to treat my CFPB submission as a dispute, Experian can not reclassify it as a customer-service inquiry in order to avoid its statutory obligations under federal or state law. Experians response explains how inquiries may generally be reported but does not address whether the specific disputed inquiries and personal identifiers on my file were lawfully obtained, accurately reported, or properly verified. A generalized explanation of policy does not resolve a consumer dispute and does not satisfy the Fair Credit Reporting Act or Washington State law. Experians handling of this matter reflects a broader process failure in which consumer disputes are unnecessarily diverted, delayed, or complicated rather than substantively investigated. By relying on boilerplate explanations, redirecting consumers between portals, and withholding source-level verification, Experian creates procedural friction that discourages consumers from pursuing their lawful rights. This approach appears designed to promote consumer attrition while protecting the credit bureaus own operational interests, rather than ensuring compliance with the accuracy, transparency, and reinvestigation requirements mandated by law. The Fair Credit Reporting Act does not permit credit reporting agencies to complicate the dispute process, delay resolution, or rely on consumer exhaustion as a substitute for compliance. Such practices frustrate the statutes purpose and undermine the consumer protections established by Congress and Washington State law. Because Experian failed to identify sources, failed to provide documentation, failed to disclose reinvestigation results, and failed to demonstrate that any reasonable investigative steps were taken after notice, Experian remains in non-compliance with FCRA 604 ( a ), 607 ( b ), 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), and 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ), as well as RCW 19.182.070 and RCW 19.182.110 ( 1 ). I am requesting regulatory review and appropriate corrective action to require Experian to correct its dispute-handling process and to delete any information that can not be fully verified in compliance with federal and Washington State law

The disputes concern collection accounts that XXXX XXXX XXXX attributes to me, including at least two XXXX XXXX accounts and one XXXX XXXX XXXX account, as well as the manner in which those accounts have been represented and the furnishers stated intent to continue reporting them. At this time, I am not asserting that any specific credit bureau is definitively reporting these tradelines. This submission is intended to place formal notice on record so that, if any tradeline from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is currently reported, reinserted, or furnished in the future, it is clear that the information is disputed and subject to accuracy and reinvestigation requirements under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. The core dispute is not limited to whether historical account records exist. The dispute concerns whether the information furnished and reported is accurate, complete, and not misleading in light of the legal status of the alleged accounts, including statute-of-limitations considerations acknowledged by the furnisher, the presentation of the accounts as active collections, and the furnishers stated intent to continue reporting them as unpaid. In its CFPB response, XXXX XXXX XXXX stated that it reviewed its records, placed the XXXX XXXX XXXX account into disputed status while requesting documentation, and indicated that it may resume collection activity after receiving documentation. It also stated that it placed accounts into a cease-and-desist communication status. In the same response, the furnisher acknowledged that the law limits how long a consumer can be sued on a debt and stated that, due to the age of certain accounts, it will not sue, while also stating that it may continue reporting the accounts as unpaid as long as the law permits. The furnisher further asserted that it is licensed in Washington but did not provide a license number or documentary proof of authorization in its response. To the extent any tradeline from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is reported, I dispute the reporting as potentially inaccurate and misleading in several respects. I dispute whether the furnisher has lawful authority to furnish and continue furnishing the tradeline. I dispute whether the reporting is complete and non-misleading given the acknowledged statute-of-limitations issues and the admission that certain accounts are judicially unenforceable, while still being presented as active collection obligations. I dispute whether the reporting implies enforceability or a compulsory obligation to pay despite the stated lack of enforceability through litigation. I also dispute whether any reinvestigation that merely confirms a furnishers assertions without meaningful verification would satisfy the requirement of a reasonable reinvestigation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. This submission is also intended to prevent inaccurate reinsertion or passive continuation of disputed reporting. If any XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX tradeline is present now or furnished in the future, I am requesting a reasonable reinvestigation and verification, including confirmation that the information meets the standard of maximum possible accuracy and does not present a misleading impression regarding legal status or enforceability. If the furnisher can not substantiate the accuracy and completeness of the reporting in a manner consistent with applicable law, correction or deletion should occur as required. This correspondence is provided in good faith to ensure accurate, lawful, and non-misleading consumer reporting and to preserve a complete regulatory record of notice, response, and compliance.

Complaint Narrative I am filing a complaint regarding unfair and misleading interest charges caused by Citibanks payment allocation practices on a credit card account with multiple promotional balance transfers, compounded by inconsistent and contradictory customer service communications. I had two balance transfers on the same Citibank credit card account : - One balance transfer with a 0 % promotional APR, scheduled to expire on XXXX - A second balance transfer with a 0.99 % promotional APR, which remained active after that date When the 0 % promotional APR expired on XXXX, the APR on that balance increased to approximately 24 %. I made an online payment on XXXX with the clear intent to pay off the balance that had just exited the 0 % promotional period in order to avoid ongoing high-interest charges. Citibanks online payment system did not allow me to choose which balance my payment would be applied to. Instead, Citibank applied my payment to the lower-APR 0.99 % promotional balance, while leaving the higher-APR balance unpaid. As a result, interest continued to accrue at approximately 24 % on the balance I was actively attempting to eliminate. This payment allocation defeated my clear and reasonable intent and caused avoidable interest. The payment screen did not clearly disclose that payments could be diverted to a lower-APR promotional balance, nor did it explain how a consumer could prevent post-promotional interest when multiple promotional balances exist. Customer Service Assurances and Contradictory Written Responses After discovering the issue, I contacted Citibank customer service on three separate occasions. During each call, I was told that the issue would be corrected, that the interest would be adjusted, and that these assurances were documented in the account notes so that any representative could review them. I specifically asked for confirmation in writing and was repeatedly told that written confirmation was unnecessary because the resolution was documented internally in Citibanks system notes. Despite these assurances, I later received written letters from Citibank stating the opposite, denying that any correction could be made. These letters directly contradicted the verbal assurances I relied upon. Copies of these letters are attached to this complaint. I am also attaching call log screenshots showing the dates and frequency of my calls to Citibank customer service. Due to Citibanks failure to resolve this issue and the continued accrual of interest, I ultimately closed the account. After closure, I no longer have online access to view the detailed interest calculations or statements. I have requested copies of my statements from Citibank for the relevant billing periods and will be provided upon receipt. Contradictory and Misleading Payment Allocation Explanation Please note that even Citibanks written responses contains internally contradictory language regarding how payments are applied. The letter states that : Each month 's minimum payment due is applied to principal balances in APR order from lowest to highest. The letter then states : Payment amounts greater than the minimum due are applied to balances with higher APRs before balances with lower rates. My payment exceeded the minimum due. At the time of payment, one balance carried an APR of approximately 24 %, while the other carried a 0.99 % promotional APR. Under Citibanks own written explanation, my payment should have been applied to the higher-APR balance first. Instead, Citibank applied my payment to the lower-APR balance and continued charging high interest, then relied on this same explanation to state it was unable to apply [ my ] payment as requested. This contradiction made it impossible for me to reasonably understand how to avoid post-promotional interest. Why This Is Unfair and Deceptive - Citibanks payment allocation practices were not clearly disclosed, particularly in a multi-promotion scenario. - The online payment system did not allow consumers to direct payments to the highest-interest balance - I relied on repeated verbal assurances that the issue would be corrected - Citibanks written responses directly contradicted those assurances- Citibanks own written explanation of payment allocation is internally inconsistent - I incurred avoidable interest despite acting promptly and in good faith Taken together, this constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice, especially when combined with inconsistent customer service representations and a lack of transparent disclosure.

narrative: This complaint concerns TransUnions failure to ensure accurate credit reporting and to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation regarding information that TransUnion is publishing on my consumer report under the name XXXX XXXX. According to TransUnions own dispute results dated XX/XX/XXXX, File Identification Number XXXX, TransUnion states that disputed information updated and other information updated and acknowledges making changes to specific fields, including Date Updated, Original Charge-Off, Maximum Delinquency, and Historical Trended Data. Despite these admitted updates, the information continues to be presented as charged off on a recurring monthly basis through at least XX/XX/XXXX. The information presented reflects that the account was closed in or around XX/XX/XXXX. A charge-off is a single historical accounting event and can not lawfully recur on a monthly basis after an account has been closed. No new activity, payment obligation, or post-closure event is reflected that would justify recurring monthly adverse reporting after XX/XX/XXXX. Reporting the information in this manner creates the false appearance of ongoing delinquency and materially misrepresents the status of the information being reported. I am not admitting ownership of, responsibility for, or liability for this account. I am acknowledging only what TransUnion is currently presenting on my consumer report and disputing the accuracy, completeness, and manner in which this information is being reported. I disputed this reporting with TransUnion. TransUnions response confirms that it altered certain background data fields but failed to correct the core inaccuracy. The information continues to appear as newly charged off each month. Updating peripheral or cosmetic data elements while allowing the primary misrepresentation to persist does not satisfy TransUnions statutory obligations and does not constitute a reasonable reinvestigation. The inaccuracy is apparent from the face of TransUnions own report, which simultaneously reflects a closed status in XXXX while presenting a newly charged-off status on a recurring monthly basis for more than five years. This internal inconsistency exists independent of any furnisher response and should have been identified and corrected through reasonable procedures. This reporting is particularly harmful because third parties who rely on consumer reports use monthly status indicators to assess current credit risk. When TransUnion reports a charge-off on a recurring monthly basis for information associated with a closed account, lenders, insurers, landlords, and employers may reasonably interpret this as ongoing nonpayment rather than a single historical event. This falsely signals continued delinquency and elevated risk where no new activity is occurring. The manner in which this information is reported also adversely affects automated credit scoring systems that rely on monthly account status and delinquency indicators. When an account is presented as charged off on a recurring basis, automated scoring systems reasonably interpret this as continuing serious delinquency rather than a one-time historical event. This results in repeated negative weighting during each reporting cycle, compounding the harm over time and materially increasing perceived credit risk for users who rely on automated scores. By continuing to publish this information in its current form after notice of dispute, TransUnion is disseminating information that is inaccurate and misleading to users of consumer reports. This practice effectively re-ages the account and unlawfully prolongs the negative impact of a single historical event. Such reporting fails to meet TransUnions obligation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act to follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy, as required by 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). TransUnion also failed to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation as required by 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ). A reasonable reinvestigation requires more than accepting or repeating furnisher data when the reporting is internally inconsistent or facially inaccurate. Information can not accurately reflect a closed status in XXXX while simultaneously presenting a new charge-off every month for more than XXXX years. Allowing this reporting to continue after dispute demonstrates an unreasonable reinvestigation and continued dissemination of inaccurate information. TransUnion has not disclosed the method of verification used to conclude that this information is accurate. I am requesting identification of the specific procedures, data sources, and steps relied upon in this reinvestigation, as contemplated by 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ). Any verification of this information must be based on competent and reliable documentation sufficient to establish the accuracy of the reporting. Such documentation would include, at a minimum, records demonstrating the actual date of charge-off, confirmation that the charge-off occurred as a single historical event, and documentation showing that no post-closure activity exists that would justify recurring monthly adverse reporting after XX/XX/XXXX. Merely restating previously furnished data, relying on automated confirmations, or repeating information that is internally inconsistent does not constitute verification capable of withstanding regulatory or judicial scrutiny. TransUnions continued publication of this information after notice of dispute increases the risk of harm and demonstrates continued dissemination of information that is known, or should be known, to be inaccurate. This conduct further violates Washington law. Under RCW 19.182.020 and RCW 19.182.060, consumer reporting agencies must ensure that consumer report information is accurate, complete, and not misleading. Reporting a single historical charge-off as a recurring monthly event misrepresents the nature, status, and credit significance of the information being reported. Continued publication of this information after notice of dispute constitutes negligent or willful noncompliance with these statutory obligations. Simply stating that information was verified while materially altering account history does not demonstrate a reasonable reinvestigation. I am requesting that Equifax : Conduct a reasonable and fully documented reinvestigation of the disputed tradeline ; Provide a clear explanation of the method of verification used, including whether the investigation was automated ; or Delete or correct any information that can not be fully and accurately verified. Please assist in ensuring Equifax complies with its obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
narrative: I am filing this complaint regarding inaccurate and unlawful credit reporting by XXXX Bank and the consumer reporting agencies concerning a XXXX credit card account ending in XXXX. I am not disputing ownership of this account. My dispute is based solely on factual inaccuracies, internal contradictions, and improper charge off reporting that appear across my credit reports. This account is being reported inconsistently across all three consumer reporting agencies. TransUnion, Experian, and XXXX each display different dates of last activity, different reporting and verification dates, different charge off timelines, different high balance figures, and conflicting account remarks. A single account can not lawfully have multiple factual histories at the same time. These inconsistencies demonstrate that the information can not meet the Fair Credit Reporting Act requirement of maximum possible accuracy. In addition, this account is being reported as Collection or Charge Off on a recurring monthly basis. A charge off is a one time accounting event, not a continuing monthly status. Repeatedly reporting a charge off month after month falsely exaggerates the severity of the account and misrepresents its true status. This type of reporting is misleading and not accurate. Despite XXXX reporting this account as charged off and reporting the unpaid balance as a loss, I have never received an IRS Form 1099 C, any debt cancellation notice, or any documentation explaining whether the debt was forgiven, sold, or retained. If XXXX is reporting a loss, it must be able to document how the debt was treated and whether required disclosures were issued. No such documentation has ever been provided. The tradeline also contains contradictory dispute status language. It simultaneously reflects that the account is not disputed, that account information was disputed by the consumer and met requirements, and that a prior dispute was resolved. These statements can not all be true at the same time and further demonstrate inaccurate reporting. I have disputed these inaccuracies previously, yet the issues persist. Minor updates, balance adjustments, notation changes, or partial corrections do not resolve the underlying inaccuracies. Unless this account is either fully removed or reported with completely identical, accurate, and documented information across all three bureaus, it remains legally inaccurate. I have retained copies of my credit reports and documentation showing these discrepancies. Continued reporting of this account without full accuracy exposes XXXX Bank and the consumer reporting agencies to further regulatory and legal action.

Following the unauthorized withdrawals, Navy Federal allowed my account to continue accruing overdraft fees, even though I had overdraft protection enabled on the account. Navy Federals actions directly contributed to my account becoming overdrawn by approximately {$900.00}, despite the overdraft protection that should have prevented this. Navy Federal is currently facing class action litigation related to improper overdraft practices, and my experience reflects the same pattern of consumer harm charging fees that should not have applied and failing to protect account holders during fraud events. As a result of Navy Federals mishandling, my account remains overdrawn, and I am now barred from opening a new account with Navy Federal due to a negative balance that exists solely because of their failure to investigate fraud and reverse improper fees. This has caused ongoing financial harm, XXXX, and loss of access to essential banking services.

The account stems from a vehicle repossession that occurred in XX/XX/year>. The loan was charged off, closed, and later sold, yet American Finance has continued to add incremental interest over the past XXXX years, resulting in a changing balance being reported to the credit bureaus. This reporting is inaccurate, misleading, and unlawful for the following reasons : 1. Improper Post-Charge-Off Interest on a Closed Auto Loan Once an auto loan is charged off and closed, interest may only continue if : The original signed retail installment contract explicitly authorizes post-charge-off interest, and Such interest is permitted under applicable state law, and The party furnishing the account has legal assignment of interest rights. American Finance has never provided : The original signed contract Any contractual clause authorizing post-charge-off interest Any documentation showing lawful assignment of interest rights after resale of the debt Absent this proof, post-charge-off interest is unauthorized. 2. Inaccurate Credit Reporting Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Despite the account being charged off years ago, the balance continues to change, which renders the tradeline inaccurate and misleading. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) and 1681i, furnishers and credit bureaus must ensure maximum possible accuracy and conduct a reasonable reinvestigation when disputes are raised. I have previously disputed this account with the credit bureaus, yet the balance has not been corrected and interest continues to accrue. This demonstrates a failure to reasonably investigate under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). 3. Failure to Provide Mandatory Auto Repossession Disclosures ( Delaware Law ) As this transaction involves a Delaware-based creditor, the following deficiencies are critical : Under Delawares Uniform Commercial Code ( 6 Del. C. 9-610, 9-615 ), after repossession a creditor must be able to document : The commercially reasonable sale of the vehicle The date and amount of sale How the sale proceeds were applied to the balance The calculation of any alleged deficiency American Finance has not produced : The bill of sale for the repossessed vehicle Proof of the sale amount Proof that sale proceeds were credited to the account A complete deficiency calculation Without this documentation, the reported deficiency balance is unverifiable. 4. Debt Was Sold Interest Rights Not Presumed This account has been re-sold, yet American Finance continues reporting interest without demonstrating : Proper chain of title A valid assignment of interest-charging authority Compliance with state and federal law Debt purchasers do not automatically inherit interest rights those rights must be expressly assigned and lawful. Formal Demand for Documentation I am requesting that American Finance be required to produce all of the following or delete the tradeline : The original signed retail installment contract The original bill of sale for the vehicle A complete payment history and ledger, to the XXXX Documentation showing post-charge-off interest authorization Proof of repossession sale, including sale price and date Proof the sale proceeds were applied correctly Proof of lawful assignment, including authority to charge interest Proof that the balance reported is accurate and lawful under Delaware law If this documentation can not be produced, continued reporting violates the FCRA and Delaware law and the account must be deleted. Requested Resolution Immediate cessation of improper interest Deletion of the tradeline from all credit reports if documentation can not be substantiated Written confirmation of correction or deletion This complaint does not acknowledge the debt and is solely a demand for legal compliance and accurate reporting.

issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
narrative: I am submitting this feedback to formally state that Citibanks response does not resolve my complaint, does not rebut my identity theft claim, and does not meet the standard of a reasonable investigation. I am also clearly stating that this submission is a new case and a rebuttal, not a duplicate complaint. My previous case number XXXX was closed, and I am exercising my right to respond to the companys explanation because the matter remains unresolved. This Is Not a Duplicate Case This submission is not a duplicate of any prior complaint. It is a rebuttal to Citibanks most recent response, which was issued after my prior case was closed. The CFPB process allows consumers to respond when a companys explanation is insufficient, inaccurate, or fails to address the core dispute. Blocking rebuttals by labeling them as duplicate deprives consumers of due process and prevents meaningful resolution. I Filed an FTC Identity Theft Report I have filed an FTC Identity Theft Report, declaring under penalty of law that I did not open, authorize, or use the XXXX Depot/Citibank account referenced in the companys response. I do not own this account. Once an FTC Identity Theft Report is submitted, continued reporting requires clear, original proof of authorization, not assumptions or internal billing records. Citibanks Response Does Not Prove Account Ownership Citibank states that its investigation determined the account is valid based on three assertions : That the information reviewed did not support fraud That I allegedly had knowledge of the debt That a payment was allegedly remitted from a valid account None of these assertions proves that I opened or authorized the account. Knowledge of a Debt Does Not Equal Authorization Knowledge of a debtespecially after it appears on a credit report or collection noticedoes not prove ownership. Identity theft victims often become aware of fraudulent accounts only after adverse reporting occurs. Awareness does not create liability and does not establish that I applied for or consented to the account. Alleged Payment Does Not Establish Ownership Citibank asserts that a payment was made from a valid account. Even if true, this does not prove authorization. Payments can be made under duress, confusion, mitigation efforts, or by third parties. A payment does not replace the need for proof of origination, such as a signed application, verified identity documentation, or authenticated account-opening records. Billing Statements Are Not Proof of Authorization The documents attached by Citibank consist primarily of billing statements and internal summaries. These documents only reflect what Citibank believes occurred after the account existed. They do not show : A signed application A contract bearing my consent Identity verification used at origination Device, IP, or KYC data tying me to the account opening Proof I received or benefited from the credit Without these elements, Citibank has not met its burden to show the account is mine. Failure to Properly Address Identity Theft Citibank acknowledges my fraud claim but dismisses it without providing the documentation necessary to overcome an FTC Identity Theft Report. This is not a reasonable investigation. When identity theft is asserted, the focus must be on how the account was opened, not on whether charges later appeared accurate in their system. Continued Reporting Causes Ongoing Harm Despite my identity theft report and disputes, Citibank continues to : Report the account as valid Maintain adverse credit information Threaten continued negative reporting if payments are not made This causes ongoing financial and reputational harm and places the burden of fraud on the victim rather than the party best positioned to prevent it. Procedural Harm From Closed Case and Blocked Rebuttal My prior CFPB case was closed, yet the underlying dispute was not resolved. When I attempt to respond, the system repeatedly flags my submissions as duplicates. This creates a procedural dead end where : The company issues a final explanation The consumer is denied the opportunity to rebut Inaccurate reporting continues unchallenged This is fundamentally unfair and inconsistent with the CFPBs consumer-protection mission. What a Proper Resolution Requires A fair and lawful resolution requires the following actions : Permanent deletion of the Home Depot/Citibank account from all credit reports Blocking of the tradeline due to identity theft Written confirmation of zero liability Cessation of all reporting and collection activity Prevention of reinsertion unless original proof of authorization is produced Acknowledgment that this submission is a rebuttal, not a duplicate Correction of my credit profile to reflect accurate information Anything less leaves the dispute unresolved and continues to penalize an identity theft victim. Conclusion I did not open, authorize, or use this account. I filed an FTC Identity Theft Report. Citibank has not produced original proof of authorization and has relied instead on assumptions, internal records, and billing statements that do not establish ownership. My prior CFPB case ( XXXX ) was closed without resolving the dispute, and this submission is a valid rebuttalnot a duplicate. I respectfully request that this feedback be considered and that the matter be resolved through permanent deletion and blocking of the fraudulent account, with written confirmation that I bear no responsibility.

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
issue: Problem with a company's investigation into an existing problem
narrative: Permissible Purpose : The law says no one can report information about me without a permissible purpose and my authorization. These accounts and inquiries have neither. There's no written agreement, no verifiable consent, nothing proving I authorized them. Continuing to report them is unlawful.On XX/XX/year>, I sent a formal dispute to Experian about unauthorized and inaccurate information on my credit report. I wasn't just making a casual complaint - I sent them everything they needed, including my Police Report ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ), which is official documentation proving these accounts aren't mine. That was over 30 days ago. More than enough time for them to investigate and fix this. But when I checked my credit report recently, nothing has changed. The unauthorized information is still there, still damaging my credit, still affecting my life. This isn't just a delay or an oversight anymore. This is non-compliance with federal law. Experian had a legal obligation to investigate my dispute and remove information they couldn't verify. They didn't do it. I've done everything right. I followed their process, sent documentation, gave them the legal timeframe. They've done nothing. That's why I'm coming to the CFPB - because a credit bureau that won't follow the law needs to be held accountable. LEGAL VIOLATIONS : I've researched the Fair Credit Reporting Act extensively, and I understand what Experian was legally required to do. Here 's what they've violated : Section 604 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681b ) - No P Section 607 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ) - Maximum Possible Accuracy : Credit bureaus are required to maintain " maximum possible accuracy. '' Keeping unverified items on my file after I've disputed them with documentation doesn't meet that standard. They're misrepresenting my credit history and they know it. Section 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ) - Duty to Reinvestigate : When they received my dispute, they were required by law to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and delete anything they couldn't verify with proper documentation. It's been over 30 days. That's more than enough time. They either didn't investigate at all, or they did and couldn't verify it but left it on my report anyway. Either way, that's a violation. Section 605B ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ) - The 4-Day Blocking Rule : This one is really clear. Once I submitted a valid police report documenting identity issues, Experian was legally required to block and delete the disputed information within FOUR business days. Not 30 days. Not 60 days. Four business days. It's been way longer than that, and the items are still on my report. That's a direct, documented violation of this section. Section 1681a ( 4 ) - Privacy Protection : I have a right to privacy of my non-public personal information. Keeping unauthorized data in my file is an improper intrusion into my privacy and causes real harm to my financial reputation. Metro 2 and CDIA Standards : Beyond the FCRA, all credit reporting is supposed to meet Metro 2 standards- meaning the data has to be complete, accurate, and current. These accounts and inquiries fail all those tests because there's no documentation supporting them and no permissible purpose for their inclusion. THE IMPACT THIS IS HAVING ON MY LIFE : This isn't just about numbers on a report. This is about my actual life being affected every single day by information that shouldn't be there : Because of this continued non-compliance, my credit score stays artificially low. I've been denied legitimate credit applications- cards I needed, loans I qualified for - all because of accounts that aren't even mine. When I do get approved for something, I'm charged interest rates that are way higher than what I should be paying. That's real money coming out of my pocket every month because Experian won't follow the law. I've faced embarrassment applying for housing. I had to explain to landlords why my credit looks bad, knowing the whole time that it's because of fraudulent information that a credit bureau is illegally keeping on my file. This situation has caused me genuine stress and frustration. I wake up thinking about it. I've spent hours dealing with this - hours I could have spent with my family or focusing on my work. It goes far beyond a " clerical error. '' This has real effects on my daily life and financial stability. WHY I'M COMING TO THE CFPB : I've acted in good faith throughout this entire process. I filed my dispute properly. I sent documentation. I gave them the legal timeframe to investigate. I followed every rule. Experian has failed to do the same. They've ignored their legal obligations under the FCRA, and they're continuing to harm me by keeping inaccurate information on my report. I'm now asking for the CFPB 's intervention because this is exactly why your agency exists- to protect consumers when credit bureaus refuse to follow federal law. I need you to ensure compliance and stop this ongoing harm.

This pattern reflects more than an isolated oversight. Equifax was placed on explicit notice of its non-compliance and given an opportunity to cure, yet chose not to respond. When I requested my servicing file, the only document provided was an incomplete copy of my note ( page XXXX only ; the signature page is missing ), not the governing servicing agreement or mortgage documentation being referenced. Due to the lack of written authority and inconsistent information, I submitted exception requests on XX/XX/year>, and was verbally advised that I would receive a response within 710 business days. No response or interim update was provided within that timeframe. My exception request was initially made by phone, at which time I was advised to also submit the request via email to XXXX and to upload supporting documentation through the insurance portal. I complied with all of these instructions. In addition to the initial submission, I sent a follow-up email on XX/XX/year>. It is also important to clarify that my initial communications beginning on XX/XX/year>, focused on payee authority concerns, due to the lack of servicing documentation provided to me and the absence of publicly recorded authority supporting the procedures being imposed. At that time, I was seeking written confirmation of who held authority over the insurance proceeds and under what policy or contractual basis those requirements were being applied. In addition to these authority-related concerns, I also requested endorsement and release of the insurance proceeds in order to pay outstanding vendors and begin repairs. Despite clearly communicating both the authority concerns and the need for release of funds through multiple channels, no timely written response or resolution was provided. Due to the continued lack of written authority and inconsistent guidance, I submitted a Qualified Written Request ( QWR ) on XX/XX/year>, seeking documentation and clarification regarding the servicing of my loan, the handling of insurance proceeds, and the authority governing the procedures being imposed. I received acknowledgment letters dated XX/XX/year>, and XX/XX/year>. LoanCare received the XXXX, and I am currently awaiting a substantive response. Despite the QWR being outstanding, the servicer has continued to impose procedural requirements and delays without providing the requested written explanations or records. The initial insurance proceeds of {$12000.00}, released on XX/XX/year>, were intended to begin reconstruction. However, at that time I had received no clear or consistent guidance regarding how my water mitigation company and moving expenses were to be handled or paid. On XX/XX/year>, my water mitigation company notified me that it intended to place a lien on my home due to non-payment. In order to avoid a lien and further harm, I promptly issued payment to the mitigation company from the {$12000.00} proceeds. This decision was made solely to prevent a lien and was necessitated by the lack of timely direction and release of additional insurance funds. As a result, I no longer have sufficient funds to pay the moving company or provide the required deposit to my XXXX to begin repairs, and I remain dependent on the release of the remaining insurance proceeds to move forward. After approximately a month with no response, I filed a BBB complaint on XX/XX/year>. Only after that escalation did I receive a response from LoanCare on XX/XX/year>. That response was a verbal denial of my exception requests, issued without any written policy authority or explanation supporting the decision. On XX/XX/year>, I was denied access to the insurance loss draft portal and received a message stating : Your claim requires special handling. We apologize for the inconvenience, but your claim requires special handling outside of the website. This restriction further limited transparency while funds remained unreleased and reviews were ongoing. Despite LoanCare confirming receipt of the insurance checks totaling {$30000.00} on XX/XX/year>, on XX/XX/year>, I was informed via phone call that funds designated for moving and transition expenses would remain unreleased and that a new review process would apply. I was advised that these exception requests would require 710 business days for review, followed by approximately 2 additional business days for processing and an additional 35 business days for payment issuance, creating delays of up to 17 business days despite LoanCare already being in possession of the insurance proceeds. On XX/XX/year>, I followed up by email with LoanCares XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to formally document this verbal update and the newly stated delay timeline. At this point, I had given notice that I intended to move forward with submitting formal complaints to the CFPB and HUD. On XX/XX/year>, I received a call from XXXX, the inspection vendor, asking whether an inspection had been scheduled. I advised the caller that I was awaiting the outcome of a pending exception request to waive the inspection requirement. The vendor indicated that they would relay this information back to LoanCare. On the morning of XX/XX/year>, I regained access to the insurance loss draft portal without any explanation or written communication regarding the status of my exception request. The portal did not provide clarity as to whether an inspection was required or whether my exception request remained under review. Also on XX/XX/year>, I received another past-due notice from my moving and storage company due to non-payment. I immediately documented this additional harm by emailing LoanCares XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and copying Lakeviews Issue Resolution team to ensure the ongoing financial impact was noted in the servicing record. Later on XXXX, XXXX, XXXX with LoanCare provided a written explanation for the continued withholding of funds. In that response, LoanCare stated that client guidelines require an inspection to confirm the status of the property before additional funds will be released, and cited inspection benchmarks tied to 50 % and 100 % completion of repairs. I responded that this is problematic because no repair or reconstruction work has commenced, as the funds required to begin work have not been released, an inspection tied to repair progress can not confirm repair status where no work has occurred, conditioning the release of initial repair funds on inspection milestones presupposing repair activity creates a circular requirement that prevents the claim from progressing, funds designated for moving and transition expenses are non-repair proceeds and, under FHA servicing guidance, are not tied to inspection or repair completion and should be promptly released, inspection availability is limited, and delays in scheduling inspections are outside of borrower control, further compounding the delay. Throughout this process, I have promptly provided all requested documentation, including invoices, a signed XXXX agreement with full scope and pricing, a valid XXXX XXXX ( which does not expire ; a newly dated XXXX XXXX was later approved but should never have been a basis for delay ), a signed conditional lien waiver, proof XXXX insurance, and a complete Encircle water mitigation report with photographs documenting work performed. All of which were now accepted and should be viewed as an approved viable repair plan. From XX/XX/year>, through the present, I have made multiple attempts via email to resolve these issues with LoanCares XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX and have also sent several update emails to XXXX Issue Resolution team requesting assistance in facilitating the release of insurance proceeds. Despite these continued efforts and escalation to senior-level contacts, the funds remain unreleased and no clear written resolution has been provided. Given the prolonged delays, shifting requirements, lack of transparency, and continued harm, I have serious concerns regarding the quality control and oversight exercised in the handling of my insurance proceeds. Additional concerns include repeated document rejections without timely explanation, initiation of an inspection workflow after mitigation was completed and paid ( despite no reconstruction having begun and no written authority provided ), fluctuating portal access, and ongoing financial harm including monthly storage fees and XXXX scheduling impacts. I escalated these concerns internally and through a BBB complaint, which received a response from a XXXX XXXX of Compliance at XXXX. Despite this escalation, delays continue and no written policy justification has been provided. I am also aware, based on publicly available complaints, that other consumers have raised concerns regarding similar servicing issues. I raise this only as contextual information to underscore the importance of reviewing whether adequate oversight and controls are in place. I believe this conduct reflects unreasonable delay, inconsistent and misleading servicing practices, and a lack of transparency in the handling of FHA insurance proceeds. I respectfully request CFPB and HUD review and assistance in obtaining timely resolution and written clarification.

narrative: On XX/XX/year> I received a cashiers check in the amount of {$3000.00} from a buyer I connected with on XXXX who agreed to purchase my piano for {$1000.00}. The buyer stated that the remaining funds were intended to pay movers on their behalf. I deposited the cashiers check at First Horizon Bank ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ). At the time of deposit, I specifically asked the teller XXXX whether the check would be placed on hold. The teller responded no. I was not informed that the funds were being made available on a provisional basis or that they were subject to reversal. The full amount was posted to my account and made available the following morning. At no point did the bank explain that availability did not constitute final settlement. Based on the banks response and conduct, I reasonably believed the funds were final and could not be taken back. Acting in good faith and under that belief, I sent {$2000.00} to the mover via XXXX transfer. The receipt is attached. On the evening of XX/XX/XXXX, after speaking with my father, I became aware for the first time that the transaction resembled a known scam pattern. This was the first indication that I might be at risk. At that point, I transferred the remaining {$1000.00} into my XXXX XXXX account in an effort to protect myself. On XX/XX/XXXX, the cashiers check was returned as fraudulent, and First Horizon debited the full amount from my account. I was not contacted or informed by the bank that the check had bounced ; I discovered this myself when checking my account. On XX/XX/XXXX, I visited a First Horizon branch and spoke in person with the branch manager, XXXX, and the teller XXXX who deposited the check. During this conversation, XXXX stated to me, I believe you are not part of the scam. However, he then stated that the bank would not file a fraud claim because this was considered a scam and therefore I was liable. Approximately thirty minutes after I left the branch, XXXX called me and advised that I send the remaining {$1000.00} back to the bank. I responded that First Horizon was legally obligated to initiate a fraud claim. XXXX stated that a claim had already been filed and that this was why he was instructing me to return the funds. I asked for the reference number for the alleged fraud claim. XXXX refused, stating verbatim, I am not able to provide that information. I pressed him on why the reference number could not be shared, and he repeatedly instructed me to call the number on the back of my debit card, without providing documentation or confirmation. I questioned whether the claim actually existed, noting that only thirty minutes had passed since I provided all relevant information and that it did not appear possible for a claim determination to have been made in that timeframe. XXXX insisted the claim existed but continued to refuse to provide any reference number or written confirmation. While I understand that Regulation CC allows banks to make funds available prior to final settlement, consumers reasonably rely on employee representations when directly asking about holds and risk. In this case, the banks response, immediate availability of funds, lack of clarification that the deposit was provisional, and failure to notify me that the check had bounced led me to reasonably believe the funds were final. Once I became aware of the risk, I acted promptly and in good faith. Despite acknowledging that I was a victim of the scam, First Horizon has treated me as liable while providing inconsistent information, failing to clearly disclose that the funds were provisional, refusing transparency regarding the alleged fraud claim, and failing to provide timely notice that the cashiers check had been returned as fraudulent.

I am filing this complaint regarding inaccurate credit reporting and debt collection practices by Southwest Credit Systems. Southwest Credit Systems is furnishing a collection account on my consumer credit reports without providing adequate documentation to substantiate the alleged debt, including the original creditor agreement, itemized billing, or evidence that the amount being reported is accurate. As a debt collector furnishing information to consumer reporting agencies, Southwest Credit Systems is required to ensure the accuracy and completeness of the information it reports. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, furnishers must not report information they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ). Additionally, once a dispute exists, furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation and correct or delete information that can not be verified ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) ). The continued reporting of this account without competent verification raises concerns that Southwest Credit Systems has failed to conduct a reasonable investigation or ensure the accuracy of the information being furnished. I am requesting that Southwest Credit Systems conduct a full compliance review and either provide proper documentation substantiating the debt or remove the account from my consumer credit reports.

narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Cash Apps repeated and improper denial of my disputes involving unauthorized electronic fund transfers, in violation of Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ). On XX/XX/year>, funds were withdrawn from my Cash App account without my authorization in connection with multiple transactions to the merchant XXXX. I did not authorize these transfers, did not make these purchases, and did not receive the merchandise associated with them. Each denial letter contains materially identical, boilerplate language asserting that the transactions were authorized because they were initiated by a device in my possession. Cash App did not provide any evidence demonstrating authorization as required under Regulation E. Specifically, Cash App failed to provide proof of affirmative consumer authorization ; evidence of customer authentication ( PIN entry, biometric verification, passcode, or multi-factor authentication ) ; merchant delivery confirmation or proof of receipt ; IP address or device-level forensic evidence ; or any documentation linking me personally to the disputed transactions beyond unsupported assertions. Under Regulation E, device possession alone does not constitute authorization. The burden of proof rests with the financial institution to demonstrate that an electronic fund transfer was authorized. Cash App failed to meet this burden. The issuance of multiple, near-identical form letters by different representatives, without individualized analysis or evidentiary support, demonstrates a failure to conduct a reasonable investigation as required by 12 CFR 1005.11. Cash Apps conduct reflects a systemic practice of denying disputes without substantiation rather than a good-faith error-resolution process. I also requested the documentation Cash App relied upon in reaching its determinations. The documents provided do not contain evidence of authorization and do not satisfy Regulation Es investigative requirements. Additionally, Cash App failed to provide provisional ( temporary ) credit during the investigation of the disputed transactions, as required under Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005.11 ). Despite timely notice of unauthorized electronic fund transfers, Cash App did not provisionally re-credit my account within the required timefram e and instead left me without access to the disputed funds while issuing repeated denial letters. FCRA 623 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) : Duties of furnishers to report accurately and correct or delete unverifiable data. FCRA 605 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c ) : Limits on reporting obsolete adverse information. FCRA 604 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681b ) : Permissible purpose to access or share credit reports. FCRA 1681n & 16810 : Civil liability for willful or negligent noncompliance. FDCPA 1692e, 1692f, 1692g, 1692k : Ban on false reporting, unfair practices, validation requirements, and civil liability. TILA 1611 : Criminal liability for willful false reporting. TILA 1640 : Civil liability for damages, including actual damages, statutory damages, and twice the amount of any finance charge unlawfully reported. By continuing to report, verify, or publish false obligations, the credit bureaus and data furnishers are in strict violation of federal law. ( 2 ) Written confirmation of deletions within 3 business days. ( 3 ) No re-insertion of deleted items except in compliance with FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) ( certification + consumer notice ). Enforcement Notice If this resolution is not enforced, I will pursue every remedy available under law, including : statutory, actual, and punitive damages under the FCRA ( 1681n & 16810 ) ; civil damages under the FDCPA ( 1692k ) ; civil and criminal liability under the TILA ( 1611 & 1640 ), including two-fold recovery of unlawful finance charges ; escalation of complaints to the CFPB, FTC, State Attorneys General, XXXX, OCC, FDIC, and Federal Reserve ; and civil action in the appropriate court. issue: Threatened to contact someone or share information improperly
narrative: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding LVNV Funding, LLC and its agent Resurgent Capital Services for violations of my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), including failure to properly validate disputed charges and continued collection activity while the account was under dispute. This complaint concerns my fourth written request for validation, all sent via certified mail. My most recent request was sent on XX/XX/year>, in which I disputed the accuracy, completeness, and legal enforceability of the balance being reported and requested documentation sufficient to substantiate the amount claimed and the authority to collect. In that correspondence, I advised that, pursuant to federal law, collection activity must cease until the requested documentation was provided. The scope of validation requested included the following : 1. A complete, itemized breakdown of the balance being reported, including : o every charge o every fee o interest calculations o any payments posted o any adjustments o dates of each entry 2. All original statements from the original creditor showing how the balance was created on a month-by-month basis. 3. A copy of the signed contract, application, or agreement bearing my signature that created the alleged obligation. 4. The full chain of title and assignment, including : o the original creditor o each transfer of ownership o documentation showing the account was legally assigned o balances at each transfer o dates the debt was bought or sold 5. Proof that the collecting entity is legally permitted to collect in my state. 6. Authentication of any documentation previously relied upon, including screenshots or system images, supported by original account records. Screenshots alone do not satisfy FDCPA validation requirements. On XX/XX/year>, I received a correspondence from Resurgent Capital Services on behalf of LVNV Funding acknowledging receipt of my dispute and stating that my inquiry was under review. Despite acknowledging the dispute, the correspondence stated that it was an attempt to collect a debt, within the same correspondence. Constituting continued collection activity while validation remained outstanding. Their correspondence was dated XX/XX/year>, yet was delivered XX/XX/year>, raising concerns regarding the accuracy of the date reflected on the letter. On XX/XX/year>, I received a second correspondence that again failed to provide the documentation required to validate the disputed charges. The documents provided consist solely of generic credit card terms and conditions and a basic account summary. These materials are boilerplate in nature and do not include the specific documentation required to validate the alleged debt, such as the original signed agreement, itemized statements detailing the charges, or proof of LVNVs legal authority to collect. As such, the debt remains unvalidated. Notably, this correspondence was also dated XX/XX/year>, despite being received a full week after the first letter. It is not reasonable that two separate correspondences, received on different dates, were both generated and mailed on the same day. Additionally, neither envelope contained postage or mailing indicia sufficient to substantiate the dates reflected in the correspondence. If the second correspondence had been sent on the date indicated, there would have been no need for the initial acknowledgment letter stating the dispute was under review. This pattern strongly suggests that the correspondence was backdated, misrepresenting compliance with statutory requirements. To date, the creditor and its agent have : Failed to properly validate the disputed charges Continued collection activity while the account was under dispute Provided misleading and potentially backdated correspondence Failed to substantiate mailing dates or demonstrate lawful compliance FDCPA 809 ( b ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) This section states that once a consumer disputes a debt, the debt collector must cease collection until it obtains and mails verification of the debt to the consumer. Due to these failures and violations, including the creditors failure to submit the requested documentation sufficient to validate the disputed charges, and its failure to provide such validation within the required statutory timeframe, the alleged debt has not been properly verified as required by law.

Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this complaint against Bank of America , N.A . regarding the unlawful retention of my business funds following the closure of my business checking account. 1. Facts Bank of America closed my business account and is currently holding a total balance of {$87000.00}, stating that the funds will be withheld for a minimum of six ( 6 ) months. The funds consist of : Approximately {$40000.00} related to merchant processing activity {$47000.00} from a separate deposited check, unrelated to merchant transactions Bank of America has explicitly stated that even the {$47000.00} deposited check funds will be held for at least six months, despite the account being closed. I have not received any check, disbursement, or lawful documentation justifying this prolonged retention of funds. 2. Why Bank of Americas Conduct Is Improper and Potentially Unlawful A. Unlawful Retention of Cleared Check Deposit Funds ( UCC Article 4 ) Under Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Article 4, once a deposited check has cleared, a bank has a duty to either : Make the funds available, or Return the funds to the customer upon account closure A bank does not have authority to hold cleared check funds for months without a court order, legal seizure, or statutory requirement. Bank of America has provided no legal order or documentation authorizing the retention of my {$47000.00} check deposit. B. Improper Use of Risk or Merchant Review to Justify Holding Non-Merchant Funds Even if a bank is reviewing merchant activity, it can not lawfully withhold unrelated customer funds. Holding non-merchant funds under the justification of a merchant review constitutes an unfair and abusive practice under : 12 U.S.C. 5531 ( Consumer Financial Protection Act UDAAP ) C. Violation of FDIC Account Closure and Funds Disbursement Standards FDIC supervisory guidance requires that when an account is closed : Remaining funds must be returned promptly Funds may not be held indefinitely without lawful authority A blanket statement that funds will be held for at least six months without providing a legal basis violates these standards. D. Failure to Provide Written Legal Justification or Adverse Action Notice Bank of America has failed to provide : A written explanation citing the specific law allowing a six-month hold Any adverse action notice Any documentation of a lawful investigation requiring retention of funds This lack of disclosure violates federal consumer protection expectations and constitutes a deceptive and abusive practice. 3. Harm Caused As a result of Bank of Americas actions : My business is deprived of {$87000.00} in operating funds {$47000.00} of my own deposited money is being held without legal justification The account is closed, yet funds are withheld I am unable to operate my business or meet obligations 4. Requested CFPB Intervention I respectfully request that the CFPB require Bank of America to : Identify the exact federal statute or regulation authorizing the six-month hold Immediately release the {$47000.00} in non-merchant deposited funds Provide written documentation supporting any continued hold on merchant-related funds Disburse all remaining balances without further delay Correct any violations of federal banking and consumer protection laws

( Cash App ) Product / Service Money transfer / digital wallet Consumer deposit account Issue Trouble accessing funds Account frozen or restricted Unfair or deceptive practices Complaint Narrative ( PASTE BELOW ) I am filing this complaint against Block, Inc. ( Cash App ) for unlawfully restricting my personal Cash App account and withholding my personal funds based on a previously satisfied business-related UCC lien that has been paid in full and terminated. Cash App froze or restricted my personal account even though : 1. The alleged debt has been paid in full ; 2. The UCC lien has been terminated/released ; 3. My Cash App account is personal in nature and not connected to my business in any way. I provided Cash App with documentation proving payment and lien termination. Despite this, Cash App responded that they will not restore access to my personal funds unless the lienholder contacts Cash App directly and provides a release notice. This demand is not required under UCC law, nor is there any legal requirement that a lienholder must contact a third-party financial service provider directly as a condition for releasing consumer funds after a debt is satisfied. A UCC lien does not grant authority to freeze a consumers personal deposit account, especially once the obligation has been fully paid and released. Cash Apps continued restriction of my personal funds : Constitutes unfair, deceptive, and abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) under 12 U.S.C. 5531 ; Represents unlawful withholding of consumer funds ; Imposes conditions that have no basis in law ; Fails to timely correct records after debt satisfaction ; Causes financial harm by denying access to my own money. Cash App is effectively forcing me to rely on a third partys actionover which I have no controlas a precondition to accessing my own personal funds, despite clear proof that no lien or debt remains.

That agreement established revised payment amounts and revised due dates for rent during that period. Any determination of whether rent was late must therefore be evaluated solely against the modified schedule set forth in the Payment Plan Agreement. This rule explicitly prohibits debt-relief companies from charging or receiving payment until a successful resolution with a creditor has been obtained. In their official response to the CFPB, Deuda Cero falsely stated that : It is critical to note that the decision to stop paying creditors was made solely by XXXX XXXXXXXX Deuda Cero and its IAPDA-certified counselors do not advise clients to cease payments to creditors, as this is a personal financial decision. Debt-relief companies like Deuda Cero routinely instruct clients to stop making payments to creditors as part of their settlement strategycreating the appearance of financial hardship to push for reduced balances. For Deuda Cero to deny advising this practice contradicts both my written proof and the very foundation of their own business model. Their representation to the CFPB was therefore deceptive and made to mislead regulators into believing they acted in compliance with the Telemarketing Sales Rule, when in fact they relied on this exact method to operate their program. XXXX and XXXX, that were also filed while I was enrolled in the program. These cases proceeded without any defense or response filed on my behalf, despite Deuda Ceros assurances that negotiations were ongoing. Stat. 454.23, which states : Any person not licensed or otherwise authorized to practice law in this state who practices law or holds himself or herself out to the public as qualified to practice law, or who willfully pretends to be, or willfully takes or uses any name, title, addition, or description implying that he or she is qualified, or recognized by law as qualified, to practice law in this state, commits a felony of the third degree This law forbids any person or entity from providing legal advice or representing themselves as authorized to practice law without a valid license. I can verify this conversation occurred, as it took place through the companys main business phone line, and I have documentation confirming the interaction. This new payment plan would have required me to pay 100 % of the account balances, since the company had failed to negotiate any reductions. It is also important to note that Deuda Ceros proposed amount was significantly higher than what XXXX had actually agreed on, the official monthly payment plan for both XXXX accounts totaled approximately {$750.00} ( {$360.00} and {$390.00} respectively ). ( Note : Please refer to image 3 for the screenshot of the Forth account transactions ) This unauthorized withdrawal constitutes a clear violation of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1693 ), which states : A preauthorized electronic fund transfer from a consumers account may be authorized by the consumer only in writing A consumer may stop payment of a preauthorized electronic fund transfer by notifying the financial institution This law protects consumers against unapproved electronic debits and requires express consent for any transfer of funds. According to their own contract, any remaining funds after termination or cancellation must be returned to the client, yet I received no refund or explanation. Of the total {$6100.00} I paid : {$3600.00} ( 59.6 % ) went to Deuda Cero and XXXX XXXX XXXX as service fees. {$1200.00} ( 19.6 % ) were unauthorized withdrawals made after I requested they stop payments. {$250.00} ( 4.2 % ) went to custodial and maintenance fees for the XXXX platform. It is therefore impossible for the program to be out of funds when the vast majority of the money I contributed was diverted to the companys own accounts rather than used for creditor settlements. Stat. 501.204 ), which states : Unfair methods of competition, unconscionable acts or practices, and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful. prohibits deceptive, misleading, or unconscionable acts in the conduct of trade or commerce. Their misrepresentations to both me and the CFPB were intended to conceal negligence and mislead consumers about the effectiveness of their services. I respectfully request that the appropriate regulatory authorities conduct a full investigation into the actions of Deuda Cero / Debt 0 Inc and XXXX XXXX XXXX, and order : Full restitution of all funds collected and withdrawn ( {$4900.00} ). Accountability for the companys false legal advice, unauthorized withdrawals, and breach of contractual obligations. Subject / Short title : XXXX XXXX & XXXX XXXX violations inadequate adverse-action notice / failure to provide specific reasons ; possible failure to provide 615 FCRA disclosures ( Request ID XXXX XXXX This correspondence constitutes a formal dispute, demand for statutory compliance, and litigation-hold notice under : Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), 15 U.S.C. 16911691f Regulation B, 12 C.F.R. Part 1002 ( including 1002.9 ) Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681m Regulation V, 12 C.F.R. Part 1022 I. Defective and Non-Compliant Adverse Action Notice ( ECOA / Regulation B ) Your adverse action notice dated XX/XX/year> states : Our records indicate that a previous credit card account that you held with Barclays Bank Delaware experienced charge-off, bankruptcy, severe delinquency, or other negative performance. This language is non-compliant with 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 ( b ) ( 2 ) because it fails to identify the specific principal reason ( s ) actually relied upon. Instead, it presents a multi-option boilerplate list and a catch-all phrase, which Regulation B and CFPB guidance explicitly prohibit. You did not identify : Which specific condition allegedly applied Which account was relied upon The relevant dates, balances, or performance facts Whether the reason was singular or cumulative Such boilerplate language does not satisfy ECOAs requirement that an applicant be informed of the actual reason ( s ) for adverse action. II. Failure to Provide Required ECOA Right-to-Request Disclosure Your notice also fails to provide the required stand-alone statement informing the applicant of the right to request a written statement of specific reasons within 60 days, as contemplated by 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 ( a ) ( 2 ) and Appendix C to Regulation B. The inclusion of a general ECOA nondiscrimination paragraph does not cure this defect. III. FCRA/ Regulation V Compliance Concerns Your notice further states : There was no impact to your credit score as a credit bureau report was not used in making this determination. This representation triggers compliance obligations under 15 U.S.C. 1681m and 12 C.F.R. Part 1022. Accordingly, Barclays must affirmatively certify whether any of the following were used in whole or in part : A consumer report from a CRA A credit score A proprietary or third-party scoring model Any third-party data source covered by FCRA If any such information was used, your failure to provide the disclosures required by FCRA 615 constitutes an additional statutory violation. IV. Formal Demand Pursuant to the statutes cited above, I hereby demand that Barclays provide within thirty ( 30 ) days of receipt of this letter : A written, itemized statement of the specific principal reason ( s ) for the adverse action, including : Identification of the specific account relied upon Dates of alleged derogatory events Balances or amounts at issue Internal notes, decision logs, or underwriting records supporting the decision Certification under penalty of perjury as to whether any consumer report, credit score, or third-party data was used, and if so : The name, address, and telephone number of the CRA ( s ) Copies of any report ( s ) or score ( s ) relied upon Score reason codes and model identifiers Identification of : The decision-maker ( s ) or approving authority Any automated underwriting system or algorithm used The model name, version, and date of execution Written confirmation that no adverse consumer reporting has been furnished in connection with this denial, or if furnished, proof of immediate correction or deletion. Re-evaluation of my application using accurate and compliant criteria, or rescission of the adverse action. V. Preservation of Evidence You are hereby directed to preserve all documents and electronically stored information relating to this application and adverse action, including but not limited to internal emails, underwriting notes, system logs, model outputs, scorecards, and backups. This preservation obligation is ongoing. VI. Notice of Escalation Failure to comply within the statutory timeframe will result in : A formal complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Escalation to state regulators, and Preservation of my right to pursue all remedies available under 15 U.S.C. 1691e and 15 U.S.C. 1681n1681o, including statutory damages, punitive damages, attorneys fees, and equitable relief.
